Subject: Private VPC staging: inference hot-path confirmation

Hi Priya,

We're kicking off the staging cutover for the EdgeOps-managed private VPC connected to Redwood's onprem inference cluster next week. Before we flip traffic, we need to confirm two things from your side:

1) The hot-path endpoints (control-plane relay endpoints, KV cache egress, and telemetry collectors) that must remain in-path for low-latency inference. A simple CSV with hostname/ip and port is fine.
2) A short staging-runbook with rollback triggers (token-level latency spike thresholds, failed health-check counts) and the single-page escalation contacts.

Can you share those artifacts or point me to where they live? If it's easier, let's grab 30m Monday (PST) to walk the runbook.

Also, please confirm if any NAT or egress proxies are required on our side for the control-plane -> telemetry uploads.

Thanks,
Mike

Subject: Re: Private VPC staging: inference hot-path confirmation

Thanks Mike — we can provide both. High level plan below and attached initial drafts: staging-runbook-v0.9.md and hotpath-matrix.csv (see attachments).

Quick summary:
- Hot-path: control-plane-relay.redwood.internal:443 (TLS), kv-cache-edge:1026, telemetry-ingest:443 (HTTPS). The attached CSV has IP ranges and failover targets per AZ.
- Egress/NAT: for telemetry we prefer outbound over TLS to telemetry.ingest.edgeops.io; no inbound NAT required from your side for control-plane calls (we initiate). If you have egress restrictions, a 1:1 NAT for control-plane relay will be fine.
- Rollback triggers in runbook: 95th-percentile token latency > 350ms for 3 consecutive 1-min windows OR >2% error-rate on generate endpoints for 2 consecutive 5-min windows -> automatic traffic-steer to hosted tier.
- Escalation: initial on-call is Karthik (infra), then Irene (platform ops), then Priya (account).

Proposed next steps:
1) You review attached runbook & matrix and confirm the IPs you see on your edge fabric.
2) We sync Mon 11/16 10:00 PST for 30m to run through hot-path failure scenarios.
3) Karthik to share NAT/egress diagram for your ops team.

If this works, I'll push a v1 to the shared Drive and send DocuSign to finalize the staging SLA.

Thanks — attaching drafts now.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Sun, Nov 15, 2026 at 09:12 AM Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Mike — we can provide both. High level plan below and attached initial drafts...

Adding the network specifics from infra side. Attached: controlplane-egress-nat-design.drawio.png (PNG stub). Key points:
- Control-plane calls originate from our controlplane-relay nodes in the customer VPC towards your edge relay on 443. No incoming connections from your fabric required.
- Telemetry upload: outbound to telemetry.ingest.edgeops.io -> we recommend allowing TLS egress to telemetry IP range (see CSV). If you must force all egress through a proxy, configure an outbound proxy with CONNECT for 443.
- KV cache replication: uses UDP for discovery (ports 12000-12010) for rapid fanout; we support TCP fallback. If your edge fabric restricts UDP, we can pin to TCP 1026 but latency increases are expected.

Failover/rollback automation notes (from infra playbook):
- Healthcheck thresholds are evaluated per-region; if region-level failure occurs, we failover to secondary region (hosted) after 90s of degraded health.
- For staged cutover, please ensure your ACLs allow the following CIDR prefixes from our hotpath-matrix (attached) and configure ephemeral ingress allowances for the staging window.

Attachments: controlplane-egress-nat-design.drawio.png (diagram stub)

I'll be on the Mon sync to walk the NAT diagram and show how sticky sessions are maintained across the fanout.

- Karthik
Lead Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
